title: Sell Mineral Rights in Rices Landing, PA
primaryKeyword: sell mineral rights rices landing pa
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Rices Landing, PA
metaDescription: Rices Landing, Greene County mineral rights owner on the Monongahela? We buy oil and gas interests in the heaviest-gas county in PA, cash offers, fast close.
heroLead: Rices Landing sits on the Monongahela in Greene County, historically a river town centered on coal barge traffic, and today it sits inside what's arguably the most heavily drilled and gas-productive county anywhere in Pennsylvania.
intro: Greene County produces more natural gas than any other county in the state, and Rices Landing families have generally had no shortage of leasing activity to point to when we ask about royalty history. If you own minerals here, the question usually isn't whether there's activity nearby — it's whether the deal your family signed years ago is still working in your favor.

sections.heading: Heavy Development Means Real Comparables
paragraphs: Because Greene County has such dense well activity, we have strong comparable data to work from when valuing a Rices Landing tract — recent royalty payments, unit participation percentages, and lease terms from nearby parcels all inform our offer. That density generally works in your favor for getting a well-supported number rather than a rough guess.

It also means a lot of Rices Landing interests are already pooled into large horizontal units with dozens of other owners, which is standard for this county and doesn't reduce the value of your fractional share, just spreads production across a bigger footprint.

sections.heading: Post-Production Deductions in a High-Volume County
paragraphs: With this much production running through Greene County, post-production cost disputes are common, and plenty of Rices Landing owners have questions about why their net payment looks smaller than the gross production numbers on their statement. We'll go through your statement with you and explain what's being deducted and why, whether or not you decide to sell.

faqs.question: Is Rices Landing in an active part of Greene County for drilling?
faqs.answer: Yes, Greene County overall is the highest-producing gas county in Pennsylvania, and this river corridor has seen sustained activity.

faqs.question: My interest is pooled into a large unit with many other owners. Does that hurt its value?
faqs.answer: No, large unit pooling is standard for this county and doesn't reduce your fractional value, it just reflects how horizontal development works here.

faqs.question: Can you explain why my net royalty is lower than the gross production value?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's typically post-production deductions for gathering, compression, and marketing. We'll walk through your statement with you at no cost.

faqs.question: Does the river access at Rices Landing affect drilling on nearby tracts?
faqs.answer: Not directly, horizontal drilling means the surface well pad location can sit some distance from your specific tract while still producing from underneath it.
